rationale: CLIMBS TO RUNG 3. Not forced — no signal fires — but chosen: seventeen passes have used rungs 2, 4, 4b and 5 and never once widened the menu, and the coverage grid says why it should now: every domain has its cells filled except the empty ones the town cannot fill (courtyard × New element, sill × everything but interaction), so the next hundred briefs from THIS menu are rotations. Thirty seconds at the wide shot, seed 42, noon then 03:00: the roofline is a third of the picture and it is inert — chimneys smoke, one vane on the clock tower points the same way in an east gale as a west one, snow whitens the slates and nothing else ever happens up there; the cross street is six cells of road with a cyclist every few minutes; the courtyard tells no time although the whole town runs on the sun. So the batch is: b80 THE CART (the bet, street, 75 min, 200-line diff invited) — a horse-drawn cart that comes down the cross street every morning, the first thing on the road bigger than a bicycle, stopping at the allotment gate to load produce and on market days at the lane end for the stalls, bringing the mill's sacks (c117) — a moving object the wide shot cannot miss. b81 THE WEATHERVANE (the new domain's first brief): the clock tower's vane turns to windSign·windF(), the chimney smoke already leans the same way, so a windy day is legible from the skyline. b82 THE SUNDIAL (courtyard × New element, the empty cell): a gnomon on the roundel whose shadow is sunVec(), so the courtyard reads the hour and the season. b83 the deck's evening (c118, life × Connect): an east arrival who stays on past eastOpen() under eveOpen() so the footbridge has somebody on it at dusk. b84 the camera's stale overlays (c119 + c120, sill × Polish). queue.brief: THE BET — take the swing: a 150–300-line diff is expected and welcome. The cross street (XS_R0..XS_R1, rows 0..64) carries nothing bigger than a cyclist (`a.kind = 'cyclist'`, spawned in spawnLaneAgent ~line 2462). Add a horse-drawn cart: its own arrival source (never a share of laneCap — spawnTapAgent/spawnCafeAgent are the model), entering from the north end of the road at a morning hour off sunUp, driving south at a slow walking pace, STOPPING at the allotment gate (ALT_GATE) where a gardener with a basket (a.crop, harvestPlot) loads it, and on market days (marketActive) a second stop at the lane end where the stalls stock from it — then out by the south edge. Draw it as two items (a body drawn before the walkers' row, the near wheel and the horse's legs after — the raised-surface law) so pedestrians read as passing it. Walkers and cyclists yield: reuse the bicycle-bell dodge. One R() for whether it comes today, hashed per day like isBandDay(); it comes most days. Name it in nameAt/personName ('the carter and his horse'). At night it does not exist. The mill (MILL, c117) has no miller — if there is room, sacks on the cart's bed on the days after a wet spell are the cheapest way to give the mill an output without an agent.

The clock tower's vane (drawClockTower, ~line 3897) is a static triangle drawn at `vane = project(..., top + 4.8)`; it points the same way in a west gale as an east one. Make it a weathervane: its arrow turns to a heading driven by windSign·windF() — pointing INTO the wind (the way vanes do), swinging through the blend windDir() so a latch never steps a frame, with a little calm-drift wobble folded from a hash the tower already has, not a new R(). Add the same vane to the church tower (CHURCH tx0..tx1) so two vanes agree across the whole width of the town; the chimney smoke (drawSmoke) already leans windDir() — after this the smoke, the vanes, the rain slant and the bunting all say the same wind. If the tower is CACHED (check drawBlocks/facades), the vane must become a live overlay drawn after the cache, projected per frame — the rose window (#81, roseLit) is the model.
